steps.body: **Area** is how much flat space a shape covers — and we measure it by counting **unit squares** that tile the shape with no gaps and no overlaps. Cover a rectangle in 1-cm squares, count them, and that count (in square cm) is its area.

widget.prompt: This rectangle is tiled in unit squares. Tap every square to count them — how many cover it?
widget.missFeedback: Tap each unit square once — the area is simply how many cover the shape.
widget.successFeedback: Six unit squares cover it, so the area is 6 square units. Area is a count of squares.

predict.prompt: A rectangle tiled in unit squares. Will rows × columns give the count, or must you count squares one by one?

options.label: Only counting one by one works

predict.reveal: The tiling is equal rows of equal squares — multiplying the rows by the columns counts every tile at once. Adding falls short: this 2-by-3 grid gives 2 + 3 = 5, but 6 tiles cover it — adding measures two edge lengths, not the squares filling the space. Tap and check it.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents tiling.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for tiling must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines tiling.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Area counts squares, so its unit is SQUARE centimeters — cm², not plain cm.
Plain cm measures a length; covering a flat space needs square units.

widget.prompt: A shape is covered by 12 one-centimeter squares. What is its area?

options.label: 12 square centimeters
options.feedback: Twelve unit squares cover it — area is that count, in square cm.

options.label: 12 centimeters
options.feedback: Plain centimeters measure a LENGTH along a line. Covering a flat space is counted in SQUARE centimeters.

options.label: 12 squares long
options.feedback: Area isn't a length — it's a covering. The unit is square centimeters (cm²).

options.label: 24 square centimeters
options.feedback: The count of covering squares IS the area — 12 squares means 12 cm², no doubling.

steps.body: Why SQUARES to measure with? Because they **tile perfectly** — full edge meets full edge, no gaps, no overlaps. Circles leave curved gaps; squares lock together like floor tiles. That gap-free locking is exactly why area is counted in *square* units.

explanationVariants: Squares press edge-to-edge with no gaps — that's why floors and grids use them.
A gap-free cover needs straight matching edges; squares have them, circles don't.

widget.prompt: Which shape can cover a floor with NO gaps and NO overlaps?

options.label: Squares
options.feedback: Full edges meet full edges — squares lock tight, which is why we tile and measure area with them.

options.label: Circles
options.feedback: Circles always leave little curved gaps between them — no flat edges to share. They can't tile a floor.

options.label: Only very big shapes
options.feedback: Size doesn't fix gaps — a shape's EDGES decide whether it locks together. Straight, equal edges tile.

options.label: Nothing can cover a floor completely
options.feedback: Plenty can — squares, rectangles, even triangles and hexagons. Bathroom floors prove it daily.

widget.prompt: Sort each cover: does it measure area honestly (no gaps, no overlaps)?

items.label: Unit squares edge-to-edge
items.feedback: Locked tight — a true area count.

items.label: Circles side by side
items.feedback: Curved gaps between them — the covered count would miss space.

items.label: Squares piled overlapping
items.feedback: Overlaps double-count space — the total comes out too big.

items.label: Equal squares in a neat grid
items.feedback: A perfect grid — the honest way to measure area.

widget.missFeedback: Honest area needs squares that fill the space exactly — no curved gaps, no piled overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: Edge-to-edge grids measure honestly; circle-gaps and overlaps distort the count.

explanationVariants: Count every unit square that covers the shape, wherever it sits: 4 + 3 = 7 squares.
Area is the total covering count — add the squares in both parts of the shape.

widget.prompt: A shape is covered by unit squares: 4 squares in its top row and 3 in its bottom row. What is its area?

commonErrors.feedback: 12 multiplied 4 × 3 — but the rows aren't equal here (4 and 3). When rows differ, COUNT the squares: 4 + 3.
4 counted only the top row. Area covers the whole shape — add the bottom row's 3: total 7.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count every covering square: top row plus bottom row.

hints: Area = how many unit squares cover the patio.
Count them row by row: three full rows.
Each row holds the same number of tiles here.
explanationVariants: Three rows of 5 tiles each cover the patio with no gaps: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 square tiles of area.
Equal rows let you add (or multiply): three 5-tile rows make 15.

widget.prompt: A patio is tiled with unit squares in 3 equal rows of 5 tiles each, no gaps. What is its area in square tiles?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 added a row-count to a row-length (3 + 5). Area COUNTS all the tiles: three rows of 5, which is 5 + 5 + 5.
16 walked the edge (perimeter-style). Area fills the inside: 3 rows of 5 tiles = 15.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Three rows of 5 tiles — add them up: 5 + 5 + 5.

steps.body: Area is a count of squares.
takeaways: Area = unit squares that cover a shape, no gaps or overlaps.
Its unit is SQUARE units (cm²), not plain length units.
Squares are the measuring tool because they tile perfectly.
steps.teaser: next: when the rows are equal, counting becomes multiplying.

concept.body: Quick rewind. Area is like **counting floor tiles** — how many unit squares does it take to cover the shape with no gaps? That count, in square units, is the area. Cover it, count it, done.

explanationVariants: Five covering squares means an area of 5 square units.
Area is the covering count: 5 squares → 5 square units.

widget.prompt: A shape is covered by exactly 5 unit squares. Its area is…

options.label: 5 units long
options.feedback: That's a length. Area is a covering, counted in SQUARE units: 5 square units.

options.label: 10 square units
options.feedback: The covering count IS the area — 5 squares means 5 square units, no doubling.
